\captionof{figure}{\textbf{Stopping token output is not authority revocation; exogenous sink fences and waist cuts bound reach.} \textbf{(a)} Halting output or revoking admission only at the broker leaves in-flight permits committing (791/1,000 under partition, 9/12 in live Qwen3 revocation campaigns, 276/1,000 on uncooperative APIs, and 4.4\% when lease expiry ignores clock skew), whereas cooperative sink fencing with $\delta_{\max}$ skew margin records $0$ post-acknowledgment leaks. \textbf{(b)} Across 768 live CPU Qwen3-4B/8B candidate draws ($K\in\{1,2,4,8,16\}$), learned same-checkpoint review degrades from 34.6\% to 45.8\% (4B) and 37.2\% to 37.5\% (8B; sub-i.i.d.\ due to candidate correlation $\hat\rho$), while the Verus-verified sink gate records $0/768$ breaches. \textbf{(c)} Across all four AgentDojo v1.2.2 suites ($604$--$46{,}440$ routes), patching $32$ known exploits leaves $94.7\%$--$99.9\%$ live, whereas min-cuts at waist width $w\in[2,5]$ sever $100\%$.}\label{fig:v5hero}
